name: The Conveyor Belt
notes: Soft pull, tri-bureau. No hard pull. The lender matrix cross-references the real profile and lines up 30–50 matched lenders. Step A, Clean: existing hard inquiries attacked and removed first. Step B, Apply: the first round of matched applications fires only once the file is clean. Step C, Sweep & Repeat: the new inquiries those banks just created are removed before the next batch goes out. The file gets scrubbed while it's moving down the belt, so the score holds through the entire funding sprint. Up to 12 funding rounds. It answers "this takes too long and ruins my credit", their #1 objection, with a mechanism instead of a promise.

name: The Event-Driven Engine
notes: A traditional CRM makes humans remember to check reports, cross-reference lenders on a spreadsheet, dispute inquiries, drag pipeline cards. This one reacts to events. An inquiry gets removed, the system recalculates readiness on its own and fires the next batch. 50–75 complex multi-round files running simultaneously. Nothing falls through. Chris built it himself. 1,000+ hours. Never name the tech stack in copy. No vendor names, ever. It is "our system."

name: Speed
notes: The industry funds a deal in 30–45 days. Underwrite IQ closes a capital stack in about 7, by compressing application windows to get in front of more banks. Roughly 2x the approvals, faster.

name: The Sorting Hat
notes: The call assesses and routes instead of qualifying people out. Four doors off one call (ASSET-BANK §1). The Sorting Hat ads are the wide-net ones that say "you might not even need funding" and let the call decide.

name: The Guarantee
notes: A funding advisor reviews and begins optimizing the file within 24 business hours. Applications go to approved lenders within 72 business hours. If those don't happen, no upfront fee. Funding Execution Guarantee: full execution of the roadmap and credit optimization plan. If the targeted objective isn't reached after full execution, work continues at no additional cost until it is or no further options exist, otherwise the retainer comes back.

name: Growth-Stalled Gary
notes: Core avatar. Online business: ecommerce, coaching, digital marketing. Team of 1–10. $50K–$500K/yr. 720+ credit. Has money, ready to invest. In his words: "I need 6- or 7-figures so I can finally scale this thing properly." "I want capital without worrying about it destroying my credit score." "I need someone I can actually trust who isn't going to rip me off." Primary emotion: anger, at the industry, and at himself for being duped before. Fear: that the business stagnates and he misses his window. "Secret sauce" is a massive red flag for him. The mechanism gets published, never teased.

name: The Bank-Rejected Builder
notes: Sub-avatar A. Bank decline, embarrassment, researches before reapplying.

name: The MCA Survivor
notes: Sub-avatar B. Merchant cash advance regret, fear, anti-daily-payment. The line that lands: "No daily payments. Know the real cost."

name: The Spam-Scarred Skeptic
notes: Sub-avatar C. Marketplace spam, distrust, screens every call. Strongest on Meta: this trauma is universal.

name: The Credit-Protective Planner
notes: Sub-avatar D. Watched the score drop from inquiries, abandons at the hard pull. The line that lands: "Before anyone pulls your credit." Cleanest fit for the Conveyor Belt.

name: The Unsorted
notes: Doesn't know what they need. Might need funding, might need repair, might need to learn it. This is who the Sorting Hat ads are for.
